edge.title: The number you say first
edge.setup: An interview goes well. HR asks your current CTC and your expectation. Whatever you answer becomes the ceiling of everything that follows — and you're being asked before you know what the role is budgeted at.
edge.tell: You're being asked to price yourself before you know what the buyer budgeted.
move: Deflect once, politely: 'I'd like to understand the scope first — what range is budgeted for this role?' Asking costs nothing and often works.
If pressed, give a researched range for the role and market, not your current salary. Your past pay is a fact about your last employer, not about this job.
Karnataka has no salary-history ban, so you may have to answer eventually — but 'eventually' after you've heard their number is a different conversation.
Negotiate the whole package: notice period, joining bonus, level, WFH days. Single-number fights are the easiest to lose.
edge.why: This is anchoring. The first number stated pulls every subsequent number toward it, even when both sides know it's arbitrary. Street smarts in a salon or a showroom and street smarts in an HR call are the same skill wearing different clothes.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'what's your budget?' from any contractor, the first quote at a furniture shop, a landlord asking what you currently pay.

lens.name: Chesterton's fence
lens.one_line: Before removing something that looks pointless, find out why it was put there.
lens.detail: A rule, a process or a fence in a field that serves no visible purpose may be solving a problem you can't see precisely because it's being solved. The discipline isn't conservatism — it's the requirement to understand the original reason first, after which you may well still remove it, but now knowing the cost.
lens.today: Cabinet has approved splitting Bengaluru's single police force into five commissionerates, and former officers have voiced concern. That is the fence question: a unified command may be doing quiet work — shared records, one chain for cross-zone cases — that no one lists until it's gone. The split may still be right; the test is whether anyone can say what the single structure was for before it comes down.
elsewhere: A weird approval step that quietly prevents a rare, expensive error.
Legacy code nobody dares delete, for reasons occasionally excellent.
A family practice that looks superstitious and encodes something practical.
lens.test: Do I understand why this exists? If not, I'm not yet qualified to remove it.

moved.what: Nandini milk is set to cost ₹8 more from 1 November, per Times of India.
moved.so_what: It's a fixed monthly cost you can see coming. Check whether the ₹8 applies per litre or per pack on the sizes you buy, and recalculate your monthly milk spend before the 1st rather than at the counter.

moved.what: Race Course Road is closed for 60 days. Separately, rain and roadworks are slowing the Hosur highway and Chandapura junction.
moved.so_what: With 45% rain chance today, treat the city centre and the south-east corridor as slow. If you cross either, leave earlier or pick a route that avoids both.

moved.what: CMRS has begun a three-day safety inspection of the Pink Line, and a separate inspection of the Bannerghatta Road stretch.
moved.so_what: Inspection is the last regulatory step before opening, so a start date may be announced soon. If your commute runs along Bannerghatta Road, keep an eye out for it rather than discovering it in the news after it opens.

moved.what: Cabinet approved splitting Bengaluru's police force into five commissionerates.
moved.so_what: Which station and commissioner cover your address could change. Find out yours now, before you need to file something and lose a day to wrong jurisdiction.

moved.what: The voter-roll revision (SIR) is being contested, with FIRs and disputes over bulk Form-7 objections reported in Karnataka.
moved.so_what: A deletion request about you can be filed without you being told. Check your own entry on voters.eci.gov.in this week, while a correction is still straightforward.

moved.what: Indian shares rose ahead of the RBI rate decision, per Reuters.
moved.so_what: If you have a floating-rate home or car loan, a rate change flows into your EMI or tenure at the next reset. Check whether yours is repo-linked, and note the reset date.

carry_over.prompt: You're offered a 2BHK well under market rate by an 'owner' abroad who shares ID and a video walkthrough but needs a token advance today, and you've not stood inside the flat. What's the tell?
carry_over.answer: Money is moving before a key has turned in a lock you touched.
